messages.g_34034f7b345a:
1. Place the flat KB base on a clear nonslip floor in front of you, centered relative to your stance. Stand with feet comfortably about shoulder width, toes slightly outward if comfortable, and the handle close enough to reach without stretching forward. Feet stay out of the base's landing area.
2. Move hips back and bend knees enough to reach the handle while keeping the learned neutral trunk shape; head follows the trunk rather than craning upward. If you cannot reach without rounding, twisting or losing balance, do not lift; choose unloaded hinge. Do not raise the bell on books.
3. Put both hands beside each other around the top handle, fingers curling underneath and thumbs wrapping to close the grips; hands must fit without forcing fingers against one another or pinching against the bell body. Keep wrists aligned with forearms. If this handle cannot accommodate both closed hands, this variant is unavailable—do not use fingertips, the bell body or one hand instead.
4. Keep arms long and the bell close to the body as you extend hips and knees together to stand. Do not curl, yank or swing the KB; stop upright rather than leaning back. Hold still briefly with natural breathing.
5. To finish while control remains, keep both grips closed and reverse: hips back, knees bend, arms stay long; lower the flat base to the original clear landing area without stepping or twisting. Both hands remain on the handle until the base is fully resting and stable, then uncurl fingers and lift hands clear. Hands never go beneath the base. Stand up empty-handed using the same hinge/knee return.

1. Face the support close enough to reach without leaning. Feet approximately shoulder-width, knees soft. While the base remains fully supported, wrap each hand around a horn near its junction with the bell body; thumbs close the grips. Do not grip only the top corners, cup beneath the base or change grips after lifting.
2. Lift only enough to clear the support, keeping the bell close; bring it to the front of the chest, elbows downward near the ribs and wrists in a comfortable aligned position. Pause before moving the feet. If this requires a heave, toe rise or shrug, return immediately: this setup/load is unsuitable.
3. With the demonstrated clear route, take one small controlled backward step and settle both feet. Do not squat while stepping. Bend hips and knees together to a shallow comfortable depth; knees follow the feet, heels stay down and the bell remains close. Stop the descent before balance, posture or load control changes. Stand by extending hips and knees without leaning backward. No prescribed deep squat or forced stretch.
4. Finish standing. Approach the same support with the demonstrated small step, keeping both grips. Place the base flat in its original space; verify it is fully supported and motionless. Only then release both hands and step away empty-handed. Use this same return after an early stop while control remains.

1. Leave the bell standing on its base beside the intended right-elbow area, away from the head. Enter the floor EMPTY-HANDED: use the checked support if needed, lower one knee then the other, support yourself with hands on the floor and settle onto your right side facing the bell. Do not descend carrying it.
2. Knees bent, put the right hand deeply through the handle and close the thumb. Place the left hand over the right gripping hand, clear of pinch points. Keep both elbows near the body. Roll together onto your back, keeping the bell close and away from the face. This is a slow side roll, not a curl or a toss.
3. Set the right upper arm on the floor with forearm approximately vertical and the bell aligned over the elbow. Keep head, shoulders and pelvis resting on the floor; bend both knees with feet resting flat. Once the position is steady, remove the left assisting hand and place it on the floor beside you. If the working wrist bends, the bell rotates or the torso rolls, replace the assisting hand and return; do not press to rescue the position.
4. Press toward the ceiling until the elbow is nearly straight, without snapping it straight, lifting the hips or pushing through the feet. Lower slowly along the same path until the upper arm rests on the floor. Keep the load away from the face. A few easy repetitions only; finish before fatigue changes control.
5. With the upper arm supported on the floor, put the left hand back over the right gripping hand. Keep the bell close and elbows near the body; slowly roll toward the RIGHT, following the exact demonstrated reverse route. Guide its base onto the original clear floor space. Confirm full, motionless base contact before releasing either hand. Do not drop it, open a grip in the air, roll away while still carrying it or stand with it. Use this same route for an early finish while control remains.
6. After both hands are free, roll away from the bell onto your side. Use your arms to reach hands and knees; move to the checked support through the empty route if needed. Bring one foot flat beneath you and rise slowly using the support. This is an unloaded exit, not part of a loaded get-up.

messages.g_b36f56e583b8:
1. The DB rests horizontally with both nonrolling heads supported in its purpose-made cradle, handle free, its axis running left–right with the two heads at its left and right ends. The initial working palm faces down over the center handle. Face the rack, feet comfortably apart on clear floor; stand close enough to reach without trunk twisting, tiptoeing or reaching over other weights. Your return space stays empty. This lesson does not load a DB from the floor.
2. With the working hand, grasp the center handle using a closed grip: fingers around the handle and thumb around the opposite side, wrist in line with the forearm. Do not grip a head or put fingers beneath a head. If the handle cannot be reached or fully enclosed, do not lift.
3. Lift only enough to clear the cradle, keep the DB close, and bring the working arm down until the DB hangs beside that thigh, with the palm facing the thigh and the heads aligned front–back. Remain facing the rack with knees softly unlocked. Do not twist, switch hands in midair, lift toward the chest or raise over the head. The other hand stays away from the DB's head/landing zone.
4. For a controlled early finish from curl/row, first return to the straight hanging-arm position described in D/E, then stand upright if hinged. Keep the grip closed and wrist aligned with the forearm. After a curl, turn the forearm until the palm faces the thigh again. Bend the elbow enough to bring the handle back to the original waist-height cradle without trunk swing; rotate the forearm with the closed grip and neutral wrist until the palm faces down and the heads regain their original left–right rack alignment before lowering onto both supports. If the cradle requires changing the grip, wrist bending or straining to restore this orientation, do not select this loaded variant at the initial equipment check. Move the DB horizontally into its supported position; fingers remain on the central handle, clear of cradle/head contacts.
5. Lower until both heads are fully supported and the DB is stable; only then release the closed grip and move the hand clear. To work the other side, put the DB down completely first, then repeat steps 1–3 with the other hand. Do not pass it across the body under load.

messages.g_c3d9ed1dd7fb: Prerequisite B-DB and a maintained unloaded hinge. Before pickup, rehearse the entire hinge, row, upright return and rack replacement with empty hands; check clearance for the head, trunk and full DB path from the rack and every other weight. If adequate clearance is absent at the start, do not assign the row. Do not improvise a backward step while loaded to create space. Pick up via B-DB 1–3, with palm toward the thigh (neutral grip). Feet remain comfortably apart, knees slightly bent. Move hips back to lean the trunk forward without rounding; head/neck follow the trunk, shoulders remain level. Let the working arm hang below its shoulder, elbow extended without a forced lock, wrist aligned; the free hand remains empty, with no furniture support. Pull by bending the working elbow up/back beside the trunk. At the top, the elbow is just below shoulder level and the upper arm approximately along the trunk's line; do not keep pulling behind that line, roll the shoulder forward, raise the trunk or twist to gain height. Lower the DB until the arm hangs below the shoulder again, keeping the hinge. For early finish, complete that lowering, stand by extending hips/knees with the arm hanging, and return by B-DB 4–5. If the hinge cannot be maintained, select unloaded explanation; no chair-supported or KB replacement is taught. Observe start alignment, elbow endpoint and unchanged trunk. Independent task: identify the first wrong action in “twist—lift chest—pull higher.” Correction/retest: rehearse elbow path unloaded with trunk still; a lighter, symptom-free observed check is separate from answering. S5; precise neutral-grip unilateral selection and early-finish route are editorial clarification, not a new certified variation.

A simple instruction error without symptoms may be corrected first with empty hands, then retested only after the instructor confirms the correction. Breathe continuously; no deliberate breath holding. No swing, clean, snatch, bridge press, overhead press, heavy/maximal lift or loaded floor-to-standing get-up is assigned.
